messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: help me to study butterfly diversity .....
parts:
Agnes:

I suggest you have a look at this paper regarding density estimation of
butterflies:

Brown, J.A. & Boyce, M.S. (1998) Line transect sampling of Karner blue
butterflies ( Lycaeides melissa samuelis). Environmental and Ecological
Statistics, 5, 81-91.


In their abstract, these authors note "We advocate that line transect
sampling is preferable to Pollard-Yates transects as a survey technique
for monitoring Karner blue butterflies. The Pollard-Yates surveys do not
adjust for differences in site detectability. As a consequence,
estimates of among-site from Pollard-Yates surveys can be biased."

A more recent paper

Pocewicz, A., Morgan, P. & Eigenbrode, S. (2009) Local and landscape
effects on butterfly density in northern Idaho grasslands and forests.
Journal of Insect Conservation, 13, 593-601.


describes the use of line transect sampling and density estimation using
Distance. The paper by Pocewicz et al. (2009) does a nice job of
showing the detection functions fitted to their data from 2 different
habitat types.

Download a copy of Distance 6.0, have a look at the users guide, and
especially the sample projects that come with the software, and that
should start you on your way to collecting and analysing butterfly data
in the field for analysis with distance sampling methods.
